Source: ServUO scripts: Services/Craft (engine and Def* systems), Misc/ResourceInfo.cs (materials); numbers and rules only

SuccessChance.Text: Every skill the item lists (Skills; the system's main skill first) must be at least its Min (the main skill's Min less the item's MinSkillOffset), using the crafter's current skill value, or the attempt is refused. Then success rises linearly from ChanceAtMin at the main skill's Min to 100% at its Max, and keeps rising past Max (above 1.0 is a sure success). The item's ChanceAtMin overrides the system's when present. ForceSuccessChance replaces the whole formula.
SuccessChance.Formula: Success = ChanceAtMin + (MainSkill - Min) / (Max - Min) * (1 - ChanceAtMin); Success = 1 when MainSkill == Max; 0 when any required skill < its Min
Bonuses: Crafting talisman for this skill: + its SuccessBonus percent (only when all skills are met)

ExceptionalChance.Text: Rolled independently of success, from the same Success value (before any clamp), by the system's ExceptionalMode. When the result is above 0 the bonuses are added. ForceNonExceptional items are never exceptional; ForceExceptional items are always exceptional when all their skills are met.

Modes.ChanceMinusSixtyToFourtyFive: Exceptional = Success - Offset, Offset = clamp(0.60 - (MainSkill - 95) * 0.03, 0.45, 0.60) (MainSkill = the crafter's current main-skill value)

Bonuses: SeriousFun crafting apron: + its ExceptionalBonus percent (AlwaysExceptional apron: 100%)
Crafting talisman for this skill: its ExceptionalBonus percent REPLACES the apron bonus
Master chef's apron: + its Bonus percent
ExceptionalChance.Roll: exceptional when Exceptional > random[0,1); only matters when the craft also succeeds

FailLosesResources.Text: A failed attempt consumes resources: normally the full amount of every resource line (All); for UseAllRes items, half of ONE batch's amounts, each at least 1 (Half). Resources listed in NeverConsumedOnFailure are kept. An equipped Master Craftsman talisman with charges keeps everything (and uses a charge). The tool loses one use either way. SeriousFun crafting aprons: Salvager keeps everything on failure, FailureSaving keeps that percent, Efficiency takes that percent off every attempt (a success always uses at least 1 of each line).

Rules.UseAllRes: Makes as many as the backpack's resources allow in one attempt (every line's amount times the count); the result stack (or a non-stackable item's uses) is that count. Skill gain is checked once per item made.

Quality.Text: Results are Regular or Exceptional (ServUO never makes low quality from the craft menu).

MakersMark.Text: An exceptional item can carry the crafter's mark when the system has MarkOption, the crafter's main skill BASE is at least 100, and the item is Markable (its type derives from one of MarkableTypes and it isn't ForceNonExceptional). The crafter chooses: always/never/ask.

Hue.Text: An item takes its material's hue when its type derives from one of ItemTypes AND the resource type derives from one of ResourceTypes, or when its system's HueOverride says so. Items that don't implement the crafting hook take the hue when they have none. Cloth-coloured items (ClothItemTypes) take the hue of the cloth used. NeverColor types never take one. ItemHue sets a fixed hue for the result.

Materials.Text: A resource line with Material: true is replaced by the material picked in the menu (the system's Materials.Primary, or Secondary when the item has UseSubRes2). The crafter's main skill BASE must be at least that material's ReqSkill. If the picked material runs out, the next one in the menu's order that the crafter has enough of and the skill for is used (SeriousFun). ForceTypeRes items convert the picked material through ForceTypeConversion.
Materials.AttributesText: Top-level Materials.<resource>.Attributes are ServUO's CraftAttributeInfo numbers (resists, durability, lower requirements, runic attribute counts and intensities...) that the crafted armour/weapon/shield gets from that material; the item classes apply them.

Rules.ResourceEquivalentsText: A resource line of the first type can be paid with any mix of the listed types (boards with logs, leather with hides, cloth with uncut cloth...).

Timing.Text: An attempt plays the craft effect a random MinCraftEffect..MaxCraftEffect times, Delay seconds apart, then resolves (SeriousFun SwiftHands apron: no delay). Only one craft at a time.

Rules.QuantityResources: Resources that hold a quantity (pitchers, kegs, bottles of liquid...) are paid from that quantity, not the item count. Beverage containers count only when they hold the item's Beverage (Water when the item gives none).
Rules.ThemePack: An item's ThemePack is only shown in its craft details; ServUO doesn't enforce it.
Rules.SkillGain: Each attempt makes a skill-gain check for every skill the item lists, over that skill's Min..Max range (UseAllRes items: once per item made, on success).
Rules.Tools: Each attempt (success or failure) uses one charge of the tool; a tool at 0 uses breaks.

Rules.StationText: NeedHeat/NeedOven/NeedMill/NeedWater/NeedMaker items need a matching world item or static tile within StationRange tiles (a square, so diagonals count) whose Z is within StationZ of the crafter's. Stations.Water also accepts the listed addons. Anvil/Forge are checked within AnvilForgeRange and also need line of sight.

CustomCraft.Text: Not an item: after the craft succeeds the crafter targets a lockable container within 2 tiles that is unlocked, movable, theirs to use and not already trapped. It gets this trap with level = floor(Tinkering / 10) and power = level * 9; the trap is armed once the container is locked (triggers on lockpicking too). Cancelling or a bad target fails the craft.
